findings.issue_text: [High/test_gap] testsuite/.../AssertEvents.java:~480 (isAccessTokenId): the grant-shortcut check is non-functional due to two defects in the same statement - the comparison is inverted (`equals` should be `!equals`) and the wrong characters are sliced (the grant shortcut occupies positions 4-5 of the 6-char prefix, substring(4,6), not 3-5); net effect is the matcher only verifies the suffix is a UUID, so expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken never actually assert the encoded grant type, and with the indices fixed the inverted condition would make every valid token fail.

[Medium/bug] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java:~76 (constructor): copy-paste error where the fourth `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` re-checks grantType instead of rawTokenId, so the intended invariant is not enforced and a null rawTokenId would silently produce malformed token IDs (e.g. "onrtna:null") instead of failing fast.

[Medium/api] server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:31: new abstract method `getShortcut()` added to a pluggable SPI interface with no `default` implementation; existing third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations will fail to compile / throw AbstractMethodError, and since DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit invokes getShortcut() on every registered grant factory, a stale custom grant jar breaks Keycloak startup entirely - a sensible `default` (e.g. derived from getId()) should be provided.

[Medium/data] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/tokenexchange/StandardTokenExchangeProvider.java:237: only exchangeClientToOIDCClient sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE; other token-minting exchange paths (user OIDC-to-OIDC exchange, SAML-to-OIDC exchange, external-to-internal exchange in ExternalToInternalTokenExchangeProvider) leave the attribute unset, so those access tokens are silently encoded with the "na"/unknown grant instead of "te", producing incorrect encoded context for a major flow.

[Medium/api] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/TokenManager.java:~1051: the access-token `jti` format changes for every issued token from an opaque UUID to a prefixed string ("xxxxxx:UUID") by default, breaking consumers that parse or store jti as a UUID (uuid-typed DB columns, client libraries, event/log processors consuming Details.TOKEN_ID); there is no version marker or configuration flag to retain the old format - internal and external consumers should be audited or the encoding gated behind config.

[Low/doc_defect] server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:~30: the getShortcut() javadoc says "usually like 3-letters shortcut" and never states a length requirement, but DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider hard-requires exactly 2 characters (fixed offsets in the 6-char prefix, `length() != 6` check) with no validation of shortcut length at registration; a custom grant following the documented contract would issue tokens whose IDs then fail getTokenContextFromTokenId with IllegalArgumentException.

[Low/api] server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java:~100: the public `Context(Context context)` copy constructor was removed from a pluggable SPI class; third-party grant code compiled against it will fail with NoSuchMethodError (binary-incompatible removal rather than deprecation).

[Low/security] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:~100 (encodeTokenId): the `jti` prefix now discloses session persistence (online/offline/transient) and grant type to every observer of the token (resource servers, proxies, logs), e.g. flagging long-lived offline tokens as higher-value targets, with no opt-out; an explicit decision is needed on whether this metadata should be exposed by default.

[Low/test_gap] services/src/test/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java:~100 (testIncorrectGrantType): the test only passes by accident - because postInit is never called, sessionFactory is null, so getGrantTypeByShortcut's lazy-refresh block throws NullPointerException which is swallowed by the overly broad catch (RuntimeException); the intended IllegalArgumentException path for unknown grant shortcuts is never actually exercised.

[Low/test_gap] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:44: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext, the production entry point classifying session type (online/offline/transient) and lightweight vs. regular token, has no test coverage; nothing in the PR asserts, e.g., that an offline session encodes "of" - the unit tests only round-trip hand-built strings and the integration assertions are vacuous.

goldens.comment: In AccessTokenContext constructor, the fourth Objects.requireNonNull validates grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId values to pass validation.

In isAccessTokenId, the substring for the grant shortcut and the equality check look inverted: the grant shortcut occupies indices 4–5 (substring(4,6)), and a match should return true (combined with UUID check), not false.

Javadoc mentions "usually like 3-letters shortcut" but some implementations use 2-letter shortcuts ("ac", "cc", "rt", "te", "pc", "ci", "ro"). Consider updating documentation to reflect actual usage pattern.
Catching generic RuntimeException is too broad. The implementation throws IllegalArgumentException specifically - catch that instead for more precise testing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/api] server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:31: new abstract method `getShortcut()` added to a pluggable SPI interface with no `default` implementation; existing third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations will fail to compile / throw AbstractMethodError, and since DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit invokes getShortcut() on every registered grant factory, a stale custom grant jar breaks Keycloak startup entirely - a sensible `default` (e.g. derived from getId()) should be provided.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut()` to the SPI interface `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` with no `default` implementation. This is a binary-incompatible change for any existing third-party `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementations compiled against the old interface. The new code in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit()` unconditionally calls `gtf.getShortcut()` on every registered `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory`, so an old custom grant factory jar would trigger an `AbstractMethodError` during startup/initialization and can prevent Keycloak from booting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/tokenexchange/StandardTokenExchangeProvider.java:237: only exchangeClientToOIDCClient sets Constants.GRANT_TYPE; other token-minting exchange paths (user OIDC-to-OIDC exchange, SAML-to-OIDC exchange, external-to-internal exchange in ExternalToInternalTokenExchangeProvider) leave the attribute unset, so those access tokens are silently encoded with the "na"/unknown grant instead of "te", producing incorrect encoded context for a major flow.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a new GRANT_TYPE attribute being set in StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient(), and that TokenManager now encodes access token IDs using clientSessionCtx.getAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE) (falling back to "na"). However, the finding’s claim that other token-exchange minting paths (OIDC-to-OIDC, SAML-to-OIDC, ExternalToInternalTokenExchangeProvider, etc.) exist and do not set the attribute cannot be verified from the provided diff because those code paths/files are not shown. Therefore the specific conclusion about those flows producing incorrect encoded context is not diff-verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/api] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/TokenManager.java:~1051: the access-token `jti` format changes for every issued token from an opaque UUID to a prefixed string ("xxxxxx:UUID") by default, breaking consumers that parse or store jti as a UUID (uuid-typed DB columns, client libraries, event/log processors consuming Details.TOKEN_ID); there is no version marker or configuration flag to retain the old format - internal and external consumers should be audited or the encoding gated behind config.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the AccessToken `jti` from a raw generated ID to an encoded, prefixed form by default: in `TokenManager.initToken(...)`, `token.id(KeycloakModelUtils.generateId())` is replaced with `encoder.encodeTokenId(tokenCtx)` where `encodeTokenId` returns `sessionTypeShortcut + tokenTypeShortcut + grantShortcut + ':' + rawTokenId` (e.g., `trltcc:1234`). The default provider is registered via `META-INF/services/...TokenContextEncoderProviderFactory` and the SPI is added to `org.keycloak.provider.Spi`, and `TokenManager` unconditionally calls `session.getProvider(TokenContextEncoderProvider.class)` with no config gate/flag shown to preserve the old UUID-only format. The finding’s compatibility concern for consumers expecting UUID-like `jti` is thus grounded in the diff, though it’s more an API/backward-compat change than an immediately verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/api] server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/grants/OAuth2GrantType.java:~100: the public `Context(Context context)` copy constructor was removed from a pluggable SPI class; third-party grant code compiled against it will fail with NoSuchMethodError (binary-incompatible removal rather than deprecation).

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly removes the `public Context(Context context)` copy constructor from `OAuth2GrantType.Context` (all the field-by-field assignments are deleted) and does not leave a deprecated alternative. Since `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` is a pluggable SPI and this `Context` type is part of its public API surface, this is a binary-incompatible change: any external grant implementation compiled against the old constructor would fail at runtime with `NoSuchMethodError` if it tries to call it. This is an API-compatibility concern grounded in the diff, not a functional correctness bug in Keycloak itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/security] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:~100 (encodeTokenId): the `jti` prefix now discloses session persistence (online/offline/transient) and grant type to every observer of the token (resource servers, proxies, logs), e.g. flagging long-lived offline tokens as higher-value targets, with no opt-out; an explicit decision is needed on whether this metadata should be exposed by default.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes access token `jti` generation from a random ID to an encoded string containing contextual metadata. In `TokenManager.initToken`, `token.id(...)` now uses `TokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(...)`, and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId` prefixes the raw UUID with `sessionType` (on/of/tr), `tokenType` (rt/lt), and a 2-char grant shortcut (from `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()`), separated by `:`. This makes session persistence and grant type derivable by anyone who can read/log the token ID. The finding is thus real and grounded in the diff, but it’s more a security/privacy/design tradeoff needing an explicit decision/configurability than a strictly verifiable correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:44: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext, the production entry point classifying session type (online/offline/transient) and lightweight vs. regular token, has no test coverage; nothing in the PR asserts, e.g., that an offline session encodes "of" - the unit tests only round-trip hand-built strings and the integration assertions are vacuous.

adjudication.rationale: The new unit test `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest` only exercises `getTokenContextFromTokenId()` and `encodeTokenId()` using hand-constructed token-id strings; it never calls or asserts behavior of the production entry point `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider#getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(...)`, which contains the new logic for deriving `SessionType` (TRANSIENT/OFFLINE/ONLINE) and `TokenType` (LIGHTWEIGHT/REGULAR) from `ClientSessionContext`/`UserSessionModel` and `AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session)`. The integration-side additions in `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId(...)` also do not validate the session/token-type prefixes and, as written, don’t meaningfully assert the expected grant shortcut (it returns false when the shortcut matches), making those assertions ineffective for covering that classification logic.
